handback.t:
STATUS: highest round completed = R65. R35 was already done by the previous director; I ran R36-R65 (R50b is a sub-entry). Everything is committed locally and nothing was pushed. Latest commit is b4da3f7. Every round is written up in RD-LOG.md, including negatives. Lib tests: 351 pass. The b1_adaptive_parity integration tests: 3 pass. I did not run the other integration tests after the last changes.

Fix to prior work: store.rs did not compile because of two literal-newline bugs, which I fixed (8ae11b3).

KEPT (all opt-in, defaults unchanged):
- R39 strict identity verifier. The shipped verifier accepted 100% of near-miss "identical" claims. The strict mode rejects 100% of them, but 0% of near-misses I authored specifically to evade its probes. That is a limit, not a proof.
- R40 MMR. It raises top-5 domain diversity only, with no retrieval gain.
- R45 fast scan kernels. About 4x faster, top-10 identical on 1,568 real queries. int8 was not faster than f32 before this change.
- R46 Rust PCA projector. Top-10 matches the python PCA exactly.
- R47 near-duplicate corpus GC. Safe, but saves only 1-2%.
- R48 shared-folder sync, measured through the real file protocol. The plain Hebbian router gains +.05 to +.06, saturating at 3 machines. The Guarded router gains about +.01, mostly not significant. There is no compounding.
- R49 BGE-base per-skill verbal profile. Vocab uses BGE, cloze uses BGE plus the cloze_mix scorer, analogies stay on MiniLM. BGE across all verbal skills was rejected because it regresses on some pools.
- R51 correctly-rounded decimal claims in the verifier.
- R52 per-table normalised lookup claims. Listing a case-sensitive table (element symbols) shows a false-accept hazard on purpose.
- R54 BM25 k1=.9, b=.5. Real-text MRR +.007 to +.011 with no domain loss. This is evidence from one real corpus of short paragraphs.
- R56 discounted foreign replay. Narrow: only the Guarded router, 4 or more machines, +.008 to +.02, confirmed on a pre-registered fresh-seed run.
- R57 HNSW ef_construction floor of 3*M. I verified that values at or below 32 lose up to 44% of clustered items.
- R59 Rust kNN capability router, with a python parity test.
- R63 combined retrieval profile (adaptive alpha plus BM25 k1/b), no loss on any axis. It gives domain world B large gains (+.08 to +.157) and real_mrr +.005 to +.010.

REJECTED:
- R36 vocab template: replicated on my new pools but flipped sign on the original B pool.
- R37 analogies templates: a true null at 5x the power.
- R41 and R50: ensemble keyword+kNN routers. Keyword rules score .36 on novel phrasing against .88 for kNN. BGE kNN is worse than MiniLM.
- R42 forgetting caps: -.04 MRR per 25% forgotten, and usage-based forgetting is worse than random.
- R43 token packing (as code); I only kept the budget table.
- R53 and R62: BGE on real-text retrieval, no gain; the BGE+MiniLM ensemble gives +.004 for 2x memory.
- R55 camelCase tokenizer.
- R60 alpha re-tune: flat optimum.

Honest corrections and caveats:
- R50b kNN exemplar augmentation is downgraded to NOT CONFIRMED. I wrote the exemplars after seeing the errors. On a fresh blind set the gain is about +.016, one item out of 60.
- The cloze_mix scorer only exploits off-topic distractors. On a hard on-topic set (24 items) every scorer is at chance, and the mix term can push below chance.
- My new test sets are synthetic items I authored, and the verbal pools are shared across seed splits.

Other results:
- R44 and R58: flat scan beats HNSW below about 15k vectors. Above that HNSW wins with M>=16 and efs>=128 (M24 at 200k). Build time is minutes at 200k.
- R61: multi-process store stress passed with no corruption.
- Headless Chrome rendered the viz HTML correctly in the light theme.

The durable store README (C:\Users\mariu\experiments\mesh-memory\README.md) documents the new commands (`meshstore sync`, `gc-docs`) and the sync and discounted-replay rules. It also states the 16-process stress result that I only logged afterwards as R61.

Next ideas: item-disjoint verbal splits; a pre-registered blind retest of the verifier and routing recipes; repeat the BM25 k1/b result on a second real corpus (long documents); update `flatq::suggest_tier` with the fast-kernel numbers; dark-theme viz check.
